rows.name: Post-harvest loss rate (%)
rows.o_value: No single national post-harvest loss rate exists. Cereals (labelled, admissible): ~10% pre- and post-harvest losses (SADS 2030, estimate c.2009); wheat losses in traditional shona storage 10-20% (FAO 2019). Horticulture:
rows.s_value: No national all-crop post-harvest loss rate is published for Egypt; the available evidence is commodity-specific and mixes loss with waste: a peer-reviewed ICARDA/ARC study estimates that 20.62 percent of Egypt's total w
rows.gate: The indicator name asserts an all-crop NATIONAL POST-HARVEST loss rate. The best Egyptian evidence sits on the wrong side of that question in two ways: (a) it is commodity-specific (wheat, grapes, tomatoes, fish), not an all-crop national aggregate; and (b) the headline 20.62 percent wheat figure is a food LOSS AND WASTAGE figure covering the whole life cycle including household/consumer wastage, not post-harvest loss alone. FAO's SDG 12.3.1a Food Loss Index — the nearest official construct, covering harvest to pre-retail — publishes global and regional values in the supplied pages (world 13.3 percent in 2023, sub-Saharan Africa 23.0 percent) but no Egypt country value appears in any page retrieved here. Those global/regional numbers are context only and are not Egypt figures.

rows.name: Smallholder access to formal markets (%)
rows.o_value: No national figure. Upper Egypt (regional, labelled): 6% of surveyed smallholder households participate in contract farming (farm household survey Apr-May 2018, seven Upper Egypt governorates, n=2,237 households; IFPRI).
rows.s_value: DATA GAP — Read all nine supplied pages in order of likely relevance. (1) IFAD 'Egypt: Smallholder contract farming for high-value and organic agricultural exports' — only front matter and table of contents retrieved; the body tables (domestic market structure, modern retail structure) that might carry a channel share were not in the extracted text, so nothing quotable. (2) and (3) FAO family-farming pages — both returned Cloudflare bot-verification screens, no content. (4) World Bank PID P180480 (2024) — contains the most on-point material, but qualitative: fragmentation 'limiting access to markets for smallholder farmers', plus the 80 percent small-scale farm-unit share; no market-access rate. (5) World Bank value-chain report (2021) — only front matter/TOC in the extract; no smallholder market-access percentage visible. (6) IFC Country Private Sector Diagnostic (2020) — front matter and figure list only; agribusiness section text not in extract. (7) FAO/CIHEAM/CIRAD small-scale family farming Egypt study (2017) — TOC only in extract; sections on cropping patterns and marketing not rendered, so no verifiable figure. (8) Egypt Ministry of International Cooperation news item — project outputs (1,200 farmers contracted, 14,000 target beneficiaries in seven governorates), a project count, not a national rate. (9) Urgenci CSA page — T5, states small-scale farmers are largely absent from Cairo farmers' markets, but no statistic and not an admissible tier for one. Dead end overall: no page in the supplied set publishes a smallholder formal-market-access percentage for Egypt.

rows.name: Agricultural credit access (% farmers)
rows.o_value: No direct '% of farmers with agricultural credit' figure exists for Egypt. Nearest labelled figures: only 2.3% of rural individuals aged 15+ had loans from formal financial institutions (ELMPS 2018, CAPMAS national panel
rows.s_value: DATA GAP — 1) Checked all four World Bank Findex 2025 Egypt pages (microdata catalog landing, study description, data dictionary F1, get-microdata) for a rural or agricultural credit statistic — these are metadata and variable listings only; the variable names 'borrowed', 'fin22a', 'urbanicity', 'receive_agriculture' appear but no estimates, and the unit of analysis is the individual adult, not the farmer. 2) Checked the Findex download-data page (worldbank.org) — it describes the availability of rural/urban disaggregation for ~300 indicators but publishes no Egypt value on the page. 3) Checked IFPRI/CGIAR 'An Agricultural Policy Review of Egypt' (T2) — retrieved text is title page, table of contents, acronym list and introduction; PBDAC is named in the acronym list but no credit-access share appears. 4) Checked GIZ Gender Value Chain Assessment (T4) — contents page lists an 'Access to financial credit' section and a sample of 100 farmers in Minya and Beni Suef, but the retrieved text stops before any figure. 5) Checked the Exa publication page on PBDAC/ABE restructuring (T5) — supply-side loan value and credit-covered-area figures only, wrong construct and inadmissible tier for a statistic. Dead ends: no CAPMAS agricultural census page, no Central Bank of Egypt financial-inclusion release, and no FAO/IFAD Egypt rural finance figure was among the supplied pages. Concluding: found=false, ratification hold.

rows.s_value: DATA GAP — Worked through the nine supplied pages in order. (1) fao.org family-farming raised beds page returned only a Cloudflare bot-verification stub — no text, dead end. (2) FAO STI Portal MRB record: rich adoption narrative and an acreage goal, but ordinal adoption levels only, no farmer share. (3) FAO STI Portal ICARDA integrated wheat bundle: adoption level '3. Project partners' — pilot stage, no share. (4) World Bank MALR programmatic support .docx: retrieved content was 'undefined', no extractable text. (5) FAO SCALA Egypt country page: NAP/NDC narrative, climate impact percentages (15 percent of Delta land affected; wheat and maize productivity declines of 15 and 19 percent by 2050) — impact projections, not adoption. (6) FAO Investment Center Country Investment Highlights No. 22: only front matter and contents were retrieved; Chapter 4 on scaling up climate-smart technologies is listed but its body text, which might carry adoption or scaling-potential figures, is not in the supplied extract, so nothing could be quote-verified. (8) Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture economic affairs crop database: page rendered as an empty query form with no returned rows. (9) Ahram Online feature (T5, and in any case statistics not admissible from this tier): quotes emission and yield-impact figures only. Conclusion: no admissible page in this set carries a percentage of farmers using climate-smart practices in Egypt.

rows.name: Women who own land (% holders)
rows.s_value: Egypt's 1999/2000 agricultural census records 236 632 female holders out of 4 537 319 civil-person holders (about 5 percent of holders female); the 1990 census recorded 285 753 female holders out of 3 470 813 (about 8 pe
rows.gate: The published statistic counts female agricultural HOLDERS (the person exercising management control over the holding), not female LAND OWNERS. The Egyptian census reports tenure (owned / rented / other) and sex of holder in separate tables and does not cross-tabulate them, so the share of women among agricultural land owners is not available. The indicator name says 'own land' but its unit '(% holders)' points to the holder-based statistic; the evidence therefore sits on the holder side of the unresolved definition question. Related context that is NOT this construct: SDG 5.a.1(b) 'share of women among owners or rights-bearers of agricultural land' exists as a global indicator (UNSD metadata page) but no Egypt value appears in the retrieved pages.

rows.o_value: DATA GAP — no rural-specific mobile broadband coverage is published for Egypt by ITU, NTRA or MCIT. Context (not scored): national population coverage at least 3G = 99.8% (ITU DataHub, 2025)
rows.s_value: DATA GAP — Order of inspection: (1) ITU DataHub 'About' page — confirmed ITU collects 'mobile population coverage (total, 3G, 4G and above)' from regulators, but the page is methodological and carries no Egypt value and no rural/urban split; dead end for a value. (2) ITU Facts and Figures 2025 landing page — narrative only ('Mobile broadband coverage is nearly universal... urban-rural divides continue to narrow but endure'), no country table, no Egypt figure; dead end. (3) Facts and Figures 2023 and 2022 PDFs as supplied — front matter, forewords and contents only; the 2023 foreword discusses income-group 5G and 3G shares globally, no Egypt row in the retrieved text. (4) Facts and Figures 2021 PDF — foreword notes 'Close to 30 per cent of Africa's rural population still lacks mobile broadband coverage', which is a REGIONAL rural figure for Africa, not Egypt, and rule 5 bars carrying it across a border. (5) MCIT 'Decent Life' page (T3) — describes mobile network coverage expansion in 4,500 villages, no percentage. (6) NTRA news release on Haya Karima (T3) — rural-specific and quantified, but in stations and villages (1096 stations, 899 villages, phase 1), not coverage share. (7) GSMA coverage-maps pages — tool descriptions only, no Egypt figure, and T4 in any case, below the tier floor for this prerequisite. (8) digitaldevelopment.org Egypt page — has 3G 99% / 4G 61% population coverage but national and T5. Not searched/unavailable in the supplied set: ITU DataHub Egypt country page, NTRA quarterly/annual telecom indicator bulletins, CAPMAS ICT statistics, and GSMA Intelligence rural coverage estimates — any of these could plausibly carry the rural split and should be the first stop on re-run.

rows.s_value: DATA GAP — Looked first for an Egyptian government artifact establishing a farmer registry: moa.gov.eg (T3) homepage returned only news headlines, one of which (28 April 2021) mentions 'collecting dairy and farmer cards' in a machine translation with no registry description; agri.gov.eg/register (T3) turned out to be a website account sign-up form for the Economic Affairs Sector, not a farmer registration portal — a dead end. The only Egypt-specific scale figures appear in Al Mal News (T5), which this row's admissibility rule excludes. Concluded: abstain pending a quotable T1-T3 source (e.g. a ministerial decree or Cabinet/IDSC report on منظومة كارت الفلاح / الحيازة الزراعية).

rows.name: National digital agriculture strategy
rows.o_value: No dedicated national digital agriculture strategy identified as of August 2026. Digital agriculture exists as components inside broader frameworks: (a) the updated Sustainable Agricultural Development Strategy (SADS 203
rows.s_value: Egypt has no separately published national digital agriculture strategy in the retrieved sources; the Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation states that its adopted Agricultural Development Strategy (aligned to Egy
rows.gate: The indicator names a 'National digital agriculture strategy'. No dedicated, standalone digital-agriculture strategy document for Egypt appears in any retrieved source. What exists, on the ministry's own site, is a digital transformation programme embedded inside the broader Agricultural Development Strategy; FAO's Egypt office page likewise lists only the 'Sustainable Agricultural Development Strategy towards 2030' among national agriculture strategies, and the FAOLEX/UNEP-LEAP abstract of that strategy makes no reference to digitalisation. This evidence therefore sits on the embedded-component side of the census's open question, not on the dedicated-document side. Separately, active digital programmes run without a governing strategy: FAO/MALR launched a digital agricultural extension model in 2019 (El Mufeed app), and ICARDA (2023) records government apps Al Mufeed, Hudhud and DAIRS as 'under development'.

rows.s_value: DATA GAP — Reviewed all nine supplied pages in order. Source 2 (CAPMAS paper to the UN Statistical Commission, T1) describes CAPMAS's legal mandate for interagency statistical coordination and notes it 'is not yet fully materialized' — statistical, not agricultural, and not inter-ministerial policy coordination for digital agriculture. Source 3 (World Bank NSDS project paper, T1) lists ministries including MOA only in an acronym list; no coordination body for digital agriculture. Source 4 (UNSD-DFID Module 3 deck, T1) carries the single most on-point sentence — an inter-ministerial committee by prime-ministerial decree — but scoped to SDG implementation follow-up; captured in construct_note as context only. Source 5 (OECD working paper on integrated governance for SDGs in Egypt, T2) is an SDG governance assessment; the retrieved extract stops at the acknowledgements and contains no agriculture coordination body. Source 6 (OECD SME and Entrepreneurship Policy in Egypt, T2) discusses cross-ministerial co-ordination for SME policy — different construct. Source 7 (Egypt VNR 2018, T3) retrieved text is front matter, contents and acronym list; the acronyms name NCCCC and NCCPIM (anti-corruption, illegal migration) but no agriculture/ICT coordination body, and no coordination text was present in the supplied extract. Source 8 (State Information Service story on PM decision forming specialised advisory committees, T3) returned a 'Page not found' stub with no substantive text. Source 9 (PARIS21, T5) describes the CAPMAS Advisory Committee for Planning and Statistical Coordination, but is T5 and again statistical. Dead ends noted: no Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation decree, no Egypt digital agriculture strategy, no MCIT–MALR joint committee document was among the retrieved pages. If such an artifact exists it must be fetched and quoted before this cell can be filled.

rows.s_value: DATA GAP — Read all ten supplied pages in order. question_4.shadow_value: DATA GAP — Order of inspection: (1) ITU DataHub 'About' page — confirmed ITU collects 'mobile population coverage (total, 3G, 4G and above)' from regulators, but the page is methodological and carries no Egypt value and no rural/urban split; dead end for a value. (2) ITU Facts and Figures 2025 landing page — narrative only ('Mobile broadband coverage is nearly universal... urban-rural divides continue to narrow but endure'), no country table, no Egypt figure; dead end. (3) Facts and Figures 2023 and 2022 PDFs as supplied — front matter, forewords and contents only; the 2023 foreword discusses income-group 5G and 3G shares globally, no Egypt row in the retrieved text. (4) Facts and Figures 2021 PDF — foreword notes 'Close to 30 per cent of Africa's rural population still lacks mobile broadband coverage', which is a REGIONAL rural figure for Africa, not Egypt, and rule 5 bars carrying it across a border. (5) MCIT 'Decent Life' page (T3) — describes mobile network coverage expansion in 4,500 villages, no percentage. (6) NTRA news release on Haya Karima (T3) — rural-specific and quantified, but in stations and villages (1096 stations, 899 villages, phase 1), not coverage share. (7) GSMA coverage-maps pages — tool descriptions only, no Egypt figure, and T4 in any case, below the tier floor for this prerequisite. (8) digitaldevelopment.org Egypt page — has 3G 99% / 4G 61% population coverage but national and T5. Not searched/unavailable in the supplied set: ITU DataHub Egypt country page, NTRA quarterly/annual telecom indicator bulletins, CAPMAS ICT statistics, and GSMA Intelligence rural coverage estimates — any of these could plausibly carry the rural split and should be the first stop on re-run.
question_4.construct_note: The closest quantified evidence in the supplied pages is NATIONAL, not rural, and sits at T5: the USAID-affiliated digitaldevelopment.org Egypt page lists 'Population covered by 3G signal: 0.99' and 'Population covered by 4G signal: 0.61' (i.e. 99% and 61% of the total population), plus '3G Coverage: 99.00'. These are national population-coverage shares of the kind the assessment's indicator census flags as the wrong side of the open definitional question: recording an ITU-style national at-least-3G number here would score level 5 mechanically while saying nothing about rural Egypt. Egypt's rural population is roughly 57% of the total, so a national 99% 3G figure is not decomposable into a rural rate without a published disaggregation, and the national 4G figure of 61% implies material sub-national gaps. Separately, the NTRA (T3) release on the 'Haya Karima' rural programme reports rural network build-out in absolute units — 1096 new mobile stations, 594 USF-funded, a 43% increase in stations serving phase-1 villages, 4G voice and mobile internet for 899 phase-1 villages at EGP 4 billion — which is rural-specific but is a deployment count, not a share of rural population covered, and covers only phase 1 of a programme targeting 4,500 villages. Neither the national percentage nor the village/station counts measures 'rural mobile broadband coverage (3G/4G)' as a rate.
question_4.abstain_reason: None of the retrieved pages publishes a rural mobile broadband (3G/4G) population-coverage figure for Egypt. The ITU pages supplied (DataHub 'About', Facts and Figures landing page, and the 2021/2022/2023 Facts and Figures PDF front matter) contain only methodology text and global/regional narrative — no Egypt country value of any kind, rural or national. The one Egypt-specific page carrying coverage percentages (digitaldevelopment.org, Source 10) is T5 by publisher and its figures are national, not rural; a prerequisite row requires T1-T3 evidence and this cell additionally requires a RURAL figure. The T3 Egyptian sources (MCIT 'Decent Life' page, NTRA news release) describe rural coverage expansion activity but publish no rural coverage rate.
